platform.name: Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)
install_commands: # Install the senzingrepo package to configure the correct apt source for your OS

# EULA acceptance — BEFORE running this command, ASK the user: 'Installing Senzing requires accepting the Senzing End User License Agreement. Do you accept the EULA? (see senzing.com/end-user-license-agreement/)' Only proceed if they confirm.
# Minimal SDK install (runtime + setup) — sufficient for SDK-only workflows
# If you cannot run apt install (containers, CI, no sudo), extract the packages directly instead:
#   Then set CONFIGPATH, RESOURCEPATH, SUPPORTPATH, PYTHONPATH, and LD_LIBRARY_PATH to point into your extraction directory.

env_vars.LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /opt/senzing/er/lib (only needed if native lib not found automatically)
env_vars.PYTHONPATH: /opt/senzing/er/sdk/python (required for Python SDK — the senzing and senzing-core packages ship with senzingsdk-runtime here)

gotchas: LD_LIBRARY_PATH is only needed if the native lib is not found automatically (e.g., custom install location): export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/senzing/er/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

setupEnv does NOT apply here. It is a POC quickstart artifact generated by sz_create_project for CLI tools only — it does NOT set SENZING_ENGINE_CONFIGURATION_JSON. Never reference it in SDK code paths.

Alternative for firewalled environments: Senzing SDK packages are available for direct download at mcp.senzing.com/downloads/ — sdk_guide returns the exact filenames and install commands when available

The senzingrepo package detects your OS and configures the correct apt source (libssl3 for Ubuntu 24.04+/Debian 13+, libssl1.1 for older). Always use senzingrepo — do NOT manually add the legacy dists/stable repo URL, which only serves libssl1.1 builds.

Python SDK: The senzing and senzing-core packages are included in senzingsdk-runtime at /opt/senzing/er/sdk/python. Do NOT pip install them — instead set PYTHONPATH=/opt/senzing/er/sdk/python:$PYTHONPATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/senzing/er/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

Evaluation mode: Without a license, Senzing limits ingestion to 500 records (error SENZ9000 at record 501). Only if the user has more than 500 records, ask for their base64 license string and add LICENSESTRINGBASE64 to the PIPELINE section of the engine config. If no license is available, offer three options: (1) continue with just 500 of their records as a sample, (2) request a free 10-day evaluation license (250K records) right now using submit_feedback with category='license_request', or (3) request a license at https://senzing.com/request-non-prod-license/. Even with a license, this single-threaded environment is not recommended for more than 10,000 records — for larger datasets, guide them to a dedicated loading pipeline.

No sudo available (containers, CI, restricted environments): First get user confirmation of the Senzing EULA (see senzing.com/end-user-license-agreement/), then set SENZING_ACCEPT_EULA=I_ACCEPT_THE_SENZING_EULA and extract packages with dpkg-deb instead of apt install. Example: dpkg-deb -x senzingsdk-runtime_*.deb /opt/senzing && dpkg-deb -x senzingsdk-setup_*.deb /opt/senzing — then adjust CONFIGPATH, RESOURCEPATH, SUPPORTPATH, PYTHONPATH, and LD_LIBRARY_PATH to point into your extraction directory.

Direct-download .deb packages: senzingsdk-runtime, senzingsdk-setup, and senzingsdk-tools are available as direct downloads. Note: senzingsdk-setup has an apt dependency on senzingsdk-tools, but when using dpkg-deb -x extraction you only need senzingsdk-runtime and senzingsdk-setup.
post_install: # Create SQLite database directory (the DB file is NOT auto-created)
# Create the SQLite database schema (required for senzingsdk-setup; senzingsdk-poc's sz_create_project does this automatically)

engine_config_notes: SENZING_ENGINE_CONFIGURATION_JSON is a naming convention used by POC tools and most official examples. It is NOT required by the SDK. The SDK just receives a string — your application can construct or load the config string any way it prefers.
CONFIGPATH: Senzing ER config files (g2config.json, sz_engine_config.ini)

Database connection string formats: internal:// (v4.3+ single-process in-memory, no setup required — cannot be shared across processes or persisted) | SQLite (dev/test): sqlite3://na:na@/path/to/G2C.db | PostgreSQL: postgresql://user:password@host:5432:g2 | MySQL: mysql://user:password@host:3306:g2 | MSSQL: mssql://user:password@host:1433:database/?driver=mssqldriver

For quick single-process dev/test on v4.3+, use internal:// as the connection string — zero setup, in-memory, no schema creation needed. Limitation: internal:// is confined to a single process via the SDK; it cannot be shared across processes, persisted, or used with external tools. For anything beyond single-process prototyping, use SQLite or a production database.

SQLite is the correct default for local testing on Linux (linux_apt, linux_yum) and macOS when you need persistence or multi-process access. The DB file is NOT auto-created — you must: (1) create the directory (mkdir -p /tmp/sqlite), (2) create the schema (sqlite3 /tmp/sqlite/G2C.db < /opt/senzing/er/resources/schema/szcore-schema-sqlite-create.sql), then (3) run the configure code to seed Senzing config. Step 2 is required when using senzingsdk-setup. If using senzingsdk-poc, sz_create_project handles all 3 steps automatically. NOTE: This does NOT apply to the pre-built Docker images (senzing/senzingsdk-tools, senzing/init-database, etc.) — those require PostgreSQL. For Docker, use senzing/init-database to initialize the database.

IMPORTANT: Without a license, Senzing is limited to 500 Distinct Source Records (DSRs). Loading record 501 fails with SENZ9000|LIMIT. Do NOT ask about licensing if the user has 500 or fewer records — just load them. Only when the user has MORE than 500 records, ASK: 'Do you have a Senzing license? If so, paste the base64 license string and I will add it to your engine config.' Then add LICENSESTRINGBASE64 to the PIPELINE section. If they don't have a license, offer three options: (1) continue with just 500 of their records as a sample, (2) request a free 10-day evaluation license (250K records) right now using submit_feedback with category='license_request', or (3) request a license at https://senzing.com/request-non-prod-license/. Even with a license, this single-threaded LLM container environment is not recommended for more than 10,000 records — for larger datasets, recommend a dedicated loading pipeline with threaded loading (generate_scaffold topic='add_records'). License options: LICENSESTRINGBASE64 (inline base64 string in config — preferred for containers/automation) or LICENSEFILE (path to .lic file on disk).
